title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continuing from p.134. X is smooth over a field K with a normal-crossings divisor D = ∪ D_i, and U = X − D. L̄ is a separable closure of the function field of U, extending K̄. The basic extension is 1 → π^{L̄}_{U/K} → E^{L̄}_U → E^{K̄}_K → 1: geometric fundamental group, arithmetic fundamental group, Galois group. Grothendieck works with the tame or prime-to-p version and writes it as a group extension.

For each stratum D_J = ∩_{i∈J} D_i, with connected components D_{J,α}, there is a 'tubular' punctured neighbourhood U_{J,α}. Its fundamental group is an extension 1 → T^J → E^{L̄}_{U_{J,α}} → E_{D_{J,α}} → 1, where T = Ẑ'(1) is the tame inertia, the Tate module of G_m. This is the Abhyankar / Grothendieck–Murre local structure. Together with the global extension it gives the commutative 'tower of exact sequences' (38) of p.134.

On this page Grothendieck analyses the homomorphisms (39) T^J → π^{L̄}_{U/K}, the inertia at points x ∈ D_J.
- Each is defined only modulo inner automorphisms of E^{L̄}_U. These come from elements whose image in E^{K̄}_K lies in the image of E^{\overline{k(x)}}_{k(x)} → E^{K̄}_K, i.e. the decomposition group at x.
- As x varies in a connected component D_{J,α}, all these homomorphisms are conjugate in E^{L̄}_U.
- The choices can be made coherently over the component. The residual ambiguity is by inner automorphisms of π^{L̄}_{U/K}, made precise by elements of the image of E^{\widetilde{D_{J,α}}}_{D_{J,α}} → E^{K̄}_K.
- The left margin gives the technical justification. Choosing a 'universal point' (base point) of U_x over K̄, compatible with specialisation, determines a geometric point of k(x) over K̄. Hence the decomposition map E_K^{K̄}-part → E_{U_x}.

Special case J = {i}. Here D_J = D_i, assumed connected, and one gets (40) κ_i : T → π^{L̄}_{U/K}. A priori κ_i is defined up to inner automorphism. In fact it is a well-defined exterior homomorphism, equivariant for the outer actions of E^{K̄}_K: on T via the cyclotomic character, and on π^{L̄}_{U/K} via the outer Galois action. This is the divisorial (cuspidal) inertia class attached to D_i.

The page ends by starting the compatibility for J ⊂ J', where D̄_{J'} ⊂ D̄_J. A component D_{J',α'} is chosen inside a component of D_J, so that the T^{J'} and T^J inertias can be compared. These lines are crossed out, and the manuscript (cote 149) ends here.

Purpose: describe the Galois-equivariant 'boundary/inertia data' of the arithmetic fundamental group of an open variety. This is part of the Longue Marche programme: Teichmüller tower, cuspidal inertia of M_{g,n}, and the Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller groupoid.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The claim that all the T^J → π maps for x in one connected component of D_J are conjugate is standard (connectedness plus local constancy of the inertia class).

The well-definedness of κ_i as an exterior homomorphism requires D_i connected, or working component by component. Grothendieck notes this himself on p.134 ('D_J connexe'), and the parenthetical on this page adds it.
The notation 'E_{U/K}' in line 6 should presumably read E^{L̄}_U; the conjugation takes place in the arithmetic group.
The compatibility J ⊂ J' is begun and then crossed out, so the page leaves the stratified compatibility unwritten.

ideas.what: Structure of the (tame) fundamental group of a punctured tubular neighbourhood of a normal-crossings stratum as an extension of π_1(D_J) by T^J = Ẑ'(1)^J
ideas.modern_name: Abhyankar's lemma / tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a NCD

ideas.what: Inertia homomorphisms T^J → π^{L̄}_{U/K} attached to points of D_J, defined up to conjugacy and constant in conjugacy class along connected components
ideas.modern_name: inertia / divisorial (cuspidal) subgroups of the geometric fundamental group
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (implicitly); Esquisse d'un programme mentions inertia/cusps for M_{g,n}

ideas.what: κ_i : T → π^{L̄}_{U/K} as a well-defined exterior homomorphism, Galois-equivariant (cyclotomic character on T vs outer Galois action on π)
ideas.modern_name: Galois equivariance of inertia classes ('branch cycle argument', cyclotomic twisting of cusp inertia)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fried (branch cycle lemma), Ihara, Nakamura; folklore
ideas.where_published: implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (Galois action on Teichmüller tower preserving inertia classes up to cyclotomic twist)

ideas.what: Base-point ('universal point') bookkeeping: a geometric point of U_x over K̄ compatible with specialisation induces a decomposition embedding of E_{k(x)} and fixes the inner-automorphism indeterminacy
ideas.modern_name: tangential/specialisation base points; decomposition groups at boundary points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions base points / fundamental groupoids with several base points

ideas.what: Planned stratified compatibility of inertia data over the NCD strata D̄_{J'} ⊂ D̄_J (tower of extensions indexed by strata)
ideas.modern_name: stratified boundary structure of fundamental groupoids / Galois action on the boundary of a NCD compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: later anabelian work on M_{g,n} boundary (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki, Ihara–Nakamura)

missed.claim: The page (the last of the manuscript) starts to formulate the compatibility between the inertia homomorphisms for nested strata D_{J'} ⊂ D_J, then crosses it out. The stratified, Galois-equivariant compatibility system is not written here. It is, however, essentially developed later in the anabelian literature on boundary/cuspidal inertia of moduli stacks.
missed.quote: (Ici, D̄_J' ⊂ D̄_J), [-Si ... D' ⊃ J ... choisissons une composante conn. D_{J',α'} de D_J ... contenue dans une compos. conn.-]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only: it documents that Grothendieck was organising the 'boundary data' of the Teichmüller tower via NCD strata and multiplicative types. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard description of inertia subgroups along a normal-crossings boundary and their Galois equivariance via the cyclotomic character. Grothendieck himself published much of it (SGA1 XIII, Grothendieck–Murre), and anabelian geometry later developed it fully. The interest is purely historical, as part of the Longue Marche working notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 6: 'E_{U/K}' is presumably E^{L̄}_U (the arithmetic group) in intent.
'moyennant [?] les chemins [?] extérieurs de π' more plausibly reads 'moyennant des automorphismes intérieurs de π^{L̄}_{U/K}', i.e. the inner automorphisms expressing the indeterminacy.
'ces [?] procédés [?] des éléments de l'image' probably reads 'ceux provenant des éléments de l'image'.
'dans un [?] fait' should read 'en fait'; 'homom. [?]' is 'homom.'.
The marginal '(Bg)' is probably '(39)', referring to equation (39) of the previous page.
Lower margin roughly reads: 'Plus précisément, le choix d'un pt. ... de π^{L̄}_{U/K} ... les opérations extérieures de E^{K̄}_K sur T ...'.
'{+dans ce cas+}' replaces a struck word before 'd'ailleurs D_J = D_i'.
